comments.text:
Please export `tools:::.split_dependencies()`. It's important for any author trying to parse DESCRIPTION files correctly, which has any number of use cases for writing tooling. I've hand-written similar logic dozens of times in subtly incorrect ways, as have other authors. I very quickly find 100 examples in CRAN packages:

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Acran+%2Fread%5B.%5Ddcf%5B%28%5D%2F+%2F%5B%27%22%5DDESCRIPTION%2F+%2Fstrsplit%5B%28%5D%2F&type=code

The function is very stable (I don't see any substantive change in 15 years). Is there any reason to keep it private? It seems like having a canonical mapping from plaintext-in-DESCRIPTION to a corresponding parsed data structure is a good tool to share.

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
If dependency _names_ is all we need, we _could_ fudge `package_dependencies` to work:

```
db = cbind(Imports="utils (>= 4.6.0), data.table, dplyr (>= 1.0.0)", Package="myPkg")
tools::package_dependencies("myPkg", db=db, which="Imports")
# $myPkg
# [1] "utils"      "data.table" "dplyr"
```

Of course, it's pretty unintuitive and drops information about version requirements.
